identity.title: MUSE-AO view of the starburst-AGN connection: NGC 7130

paper_type_evidence.quote: We use additional data from the literature: an archival WFPC3 F555W *HST* image, 600 s deep (6 different exposures)
and the ALMA CO(6-5) data with a $0.20\ensuremath{''}\times0.14\ensuremath{''}$ resolution from (cite: Zhao2016)

evidence.quote: a peculiar Sa (cite: deVaucouleurs1991) galaxy at a distance of 65.5 Mpc (so $1^{\prime\prime}$ corresponds to 318 pc)

question.value: What does the first AO-assisted MUSE NFM view of the composite AGN-starburst galaxy NGC 7130 reveal about its circumnuclear structure, line ratios and kinematics?

evidence.quote: In this Letter, we present the first results from the science verification phase of MUSE-NFM (narrow field mode)
This Letter makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00524.S.
the ALMA CO(6-5) data with a $0.20\ensuremath{''}\times0.14\ensuremath{''}$ resolution from (cite: Zhao2016)
the ALMA CO(6-5) data with a $0.20\ensuremath{''}\times0.14\ensuremath{''}$ resolution from (cite: Zhao2016)
We used the MUSE integral field spectrograph on the VLT in its newly commissioned NFM in conjunction with GALACSI
an archival WFPC3 F555W *HST* image, 600 s deep (6 different exposures)

provided.value: Astrometric calibration of HST and MUSE

evidence.quote: We calibrated the astrometry for the *HST* and the MUSE data by comparing the position of SF knots with their coordinates in the Gaia DR2

what.value: ALMA CO(6-5) data of NGC 7130 at 0.20"x0.14"

evidence.quote: the ALMA CO(6-5) data with a $0.20\ensuremath{''}\times0.14\ensuremath{''}$ resolution from (cite: Zhao2016)
We adopted as radial velocity of the galaxy the value of 4799 km s$^{-1}$ from Zhao et al. (2016).

archive_products_used_as_is.value: ALMA data used as published by Zhao et al. 2016; no astrometric calibration needed

evidence.quote: The ALMA data have good astrometry, so no calibration was required for those.
we followed the procedure in Comerón et al. (2019, submitted), based on that used for MaNGA

what.value: eta parameter for diagnostic diagram mapping

evidence.quote: using the parameter $\eta$ as introduced by Erroz-Ferrer et al. (2019, submitted)
whose size we measure here following the methodology of (cite: Comeron2014)

unstated_but_needed: ALMA calibration and imaging details (all deferred to Zhao et al. 2016)
How the ALMA moment maps were made and overlaid
The CO(6-5) flux or other measured values from ALMA
Dust and extinction details used for ALMA comparison

used_for.value: MUSE data reduction under ESO REFLEX

evidence.quote: The resulting data were reduced using v. 2.5.2 of the MUSE pipeline (cite: Weilbacher2012) under the ESO REFLEX interface
We fitted the stellar component in the spectra obtained from the ST using `pPXF` (cite: Cappellari2004; Cappellari2017).
produced two spatial Voronoi binnings using the software by (cite: Cappellari2003)
a ring configuration with a radius of $0.58\ensuremath{''}$ (185 pc; outlined in Fig. [1](#fig1))
The spatial resolution of our MUSE data is around $0.15\ensuremath{''}$.

findings_qualitative.value: A plume of AGN-like emission and high velocity dispersion extends NW from the nucleus, interpreted as an outflow with no counterpart in CO(6-5).

evidence.quote: The plume towards the NW does not have a counterpart in either UV, optical, or IR imaging (cite: Gonzalez_Delgado1998; Davies2014), nor in CO(6-5) (cite: Zhao2016).

claims.hypothesis: AO-assisted MUSE NFM reveals new structure in the circumnuclear region of NGC 7130
claims.experiment: MUSE NFM IFU observations, emission-line fitting, diagnostic diagrams, kinematic maps
claims.result: A ~0.2" radius kinematically decoupled nuclear disc and a ~640 pc AGN-like plume were found
claims.finding: Two discoveries: a tiny decoupled nuclear disc and an AGN-driven outflow plume

evidence.quote: has led to two discoveries.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: The nuclear velocity feature may be a jet-connected structure rather than a disc, though the two interpretations are compatible.

evidence.quote: although an alternative interpretation as a tiny nuclear disc rotating in a different plane from the host galaxy would not be at odds with the jet explanation.

limitations_admitted.value: Absolute flux calibration may change with a pipeline update.

evidence.quote: This update may affect the absolute flux calibration, so we warn that the values given here may have to be updated later.

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA is only a comparison dataset; no new ALMA analysis is done
Plume interpreted as a jet without independent confirmation
The conclusions text says NE while the main text says NW

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA data are archival/literature; MUSE from ESO programme 60.A-9493(A)

evidence.quote: We use additional data from the literature

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~10s of GB for MUSE; ALMA CO(6-5) ~ few GB
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA role is minimal; the ALMA data are used only as a literature comparison and no ALMA processing is described.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The main results are MUSE-based and qualitative; the ALMA role is minor.
